people.name: Courtney Barnett
people.description: Australian singer, songwriter Courtney Barnett. She released her debut album Sometimes I Sit and Think, and Sometimes I Just Sit in 2015. At the 2015 ARIA Music Awards, she won four awards from eight nominations.

people.name: Mick Thomson
people.description: Mick Thomson lead guitarist in the metal band Slipknot, in which he is designated #7. Slipknot is well known for its attention-grabbing image, aggressive style of music, and energetic and chaotic live shows.

people.name: Robert Miles
people.description: Swiss-born Italian record producer, composer, musician and DJ Robert Miles, who had the 1996 UK No.2 single 'Children'. Miles died in Ibiza, Spain, on 9 May 2017 at the age of 47 after a 9-month battle with stage 4 metastatic cancer.

people.name: Mark Roberts
people.description: Mark Roberts, guitarist with the alternative rock band from Wales, Catatonia who had the 1998 UK No.3 single 'Mulder And Scully'. The song makes direct reference to fictional FBI special agents Fox Mulder (David Duchovny) and Dana Scully (Gillian Anderson), the two main characters of the popular sci-fi TV series The X-Files.

people.name: Steven Wilson
people.description: English musician Steven Wilson, the founder, guitarist, lead vocalist, and songwriter of the rock band Porcupine Tree, as well as being a member of several other bands, including Blackfield, Storm Corrosion and No-Man.

people.name: Marilyn
people.description: English singer Marilyn known for his androgynous appearance. He was one of Britain's most successful gender bending musical artists in the 1980s. First becoming a noted figure on the London club scene, Marilyn topped the European, Japanese and Australian charts with his 1983 UK No.4 single 'Calling Your Name'. Marilyn also contributed to the Christmas number one Band Aid song, 'Do They Know It's Christmas?'

people.name: Ian McNabb
people.description: English singer-songwriter and musician Ian McNabb, previously the frontman of the Icicle Works who had the 1984 UK No.15 single 'Love Is A Wonderful Colour' and they also hit the top 40 in the United States and Canada with the single 'Whisper to a Scream (Birds Fly)' in 1984. McNabb has since embarked on a solo career and has performed with Ringo Starr, Crazy Horse, Mike Scott (of the Waterboys), and Danny Thompson of folk band Pentangle.

people.name: James Prime
people.description: Scottish musician and keyboardist James Prime, who with Deacon Blue had the 1988 UK No.8 single 'Real Gone Kid', plus over 15 other UK Top 40 singles. He featured on all eleven of their studio albums, the most recent, The Great Western Road (2025), released three months prior to his death. Before joining Deacon Blue in 1985, he had worked with Scottish band Altered Images. Prime died following a short battle with cancer on 19 June 2025, at the age of 64.

people.name: Adam Ant
people.description: English singer and musician Stuart Goddard, (Adam Ant), who had the 1981 UK No.1 single 'Stand And Deliver' with Adam and the Ants. He scored 10 UK top ten hits from 1980 to 1983, including three UK No.1 singles. He has also worked as an actor, appearing in over two dozen films and television episodes from 1985 to 2003.

people.name: Del Palmer
people.description: English musician and sound engineer Del Palmer. He is best known for his work with Kate Bush, with whom he also had a long-term personal relationship from the late 1970s to the early 1990s. Palmer was credited as an engineer on Kate Bush's Hounds of Love (1985), The Sensual World (1989), The Red Shoes (1993) and Aerial (2005). He released his first solo studio album titled Leap of Faith in 2007. He died on 5 January 2024 at the age of 71.

people.name: Lulu
people.description: Scottish singer, songwriter, actress and television personality Lulu, (Marie Lawrie), who had the 1964 UK No.7 single 'Shout' plus over 10 other UK Top 40 and the 1967 US No.1 single 'To Sir With Love'. During the 1960s, she achieved another five top-ten hits on the UK Singles Chart, including 'Boom Bang-a-Bang', which won the Eurovision Song Contest in 1969. In the late 1960s, Lulu's pop career in the UK thrived, and she had several television series of her own. In 1974, she sang the title song for the James Bond film The Man with the Golden Gun. She scored the 1993 UK No.1 'Relight My Fire' with Take That.

people.name: Tommy Dee
people.description: Tommy Dee, from John Fred and His Playboy Band who had the 1968 US No.1 & UK No.3 single 'Judy in Disguise (With Glasses)' which was a parodic play on the title of The Beatles' song 'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds'.

people.name: Nick Simper
people.description: Nick Simper, English bass guitarist with Johnny Kidd & The Pirates, The Flower Pot Men, and Lord Sutch's Savages. Simper was in the 1966 car crash that Killed Johnny Kid, became a founder member of Deep Purple. He quit the band in 1969.

people.name: Bob Nave
people.description: Keyboardist Bob Nave from American psychedelic rock band The Lemon Pipers known for their song 'Green Tambourine', which reached No. 1 in the United States in 1968. The song has been credited as being the first bubblegum pop chart-topper. Nave died on 28 January 2020, at the age of 75.

people.name: Bert Jansch
people.description: Scottish folk musician Bert Jansch, who was a songwriter and guitarist with Pentangle, John Renbourn and worked as a solo artist. Jansch was a leading figure in the 1960s British folk revival. Jansch died on 5 October 2011, aged 67, after a long battle with lung cancer.

people.name: John Barry
people.description: English composer and conductor John Barry. He composed the scores for 11 of the James Bond films between 1963 and 1987. He wrote the Grammy- and Academy Award-winning scores to the films Dances with Wolves and Out of Africa, as well as the theme for the British television cult series The Persuaders! Barry died of a heart attack on 31st January 2011 aged 77.

people.name: Mable John
people.description: American blues vocalist Mable John, the first female signed by Berry Gordy to Motown's Tamla label. After leaving Motown, John spent several years as a Raelette, backing many Ray Charles hits. She died in Los Angeles on 25 August 2022, at the age of 91.

works.title: Soul Bossa Nova
works.eventDescription: American record producer, composer and musician Quincy Jones died from pancreatic cancer aged 91. He was known for his 1962 tune 'Soul Bossa Nova' and later scored the 1978 US No.1 single 'Stuff Like That'. Jones has a record 79 Grammy Award nominations and was the producer of three albums by Michael Jackson, Off The Wall, Bad and Thriller which has now sold more than 65 million copies worldwide.

A re-recording the Taylor Swift crossover pop album 1989 became the UK's fastest-selling record of 2023. 1989 (Taylor's Version) sold 184,000 copies in one week. In the US the album sold 1.1 million copies since its release and 580,000 were on vinyl - the largest week for a single album in that format since modern sales tracking began in 1991.

works.title: I Knew You Were Trouble
works.eventDescription: The first ever YouTube awards were held in New York City. The event featured Eminem, Lady Gaga and M.I.A making live music videos directed by the awards' creator, Spike Jonze, and others. Eminem won Artist of the Year, while Taylor Swift's 'I Knew You Were Trouble' took the YouTube Phenomenon award.

works.title: Speed of Sound
works.eventDescription: Winners at this years MTV Europe awards included Coldplay who won best UK act and best song for 'Speed Of Sound’, Green Day won best rock act and best album, Alicia Keys was named best R&B act, System of a Down won best alternative act, The Black Eyed Peas won the best pop award and for the first time, the awards included a category for best African act, won by 2 Face. Madonna, in her first live TV performance since a riding accident, launched the show by emerging from a giant disco ball. Madonna also presented MTV's 'Free Your Mind' humanitarian award to Live 8 organiser Bob Geldof.

works.title: Does Your Chewing Gum Lose Its Flavour?
works.eventDescription: Lonnie Donegan, died mid-way through a UK tour and shortly before he was due to perform at a memorial concert for George Harrison with The Rolling Stones. He was aged 71. Donegan who launched the skiffle craze in the UK had the 1959 hit ‘Does Your Chewing Gum Lose Its Flavour’, the 1960 UK No.1 single 'My Old Man's A Dustman', 'Rock Island Line', plus over 30 other UK Top 40 singles.

works.title: Only Want to Be With You
works.eventDescription: Hootie and the Blowfish reached an out of court settlement with Bob Dylan for the group's unauthorized use of Dylan's lyrics in their song 'Only Want To Be With You'.

works.title: Keep the Faith
works.eventDescription: Bon Jovi released their fifth studio album, Keep The Faith, which spent a total of 49 weeks on the US chart. The album produced three Top 40 hits: 'Keep The Faith', 'Bed of Roses' and 'In These Arms'.

works.title: Unchained Melody
works.eventDescription: 25 years after their version was recorded, The Righteous Brothers went to No.1 on the UK singles chart with Unchained Melody. The track had been featured in the Patrick Swayze film Ghost. Written by Alex North and Hy Zaret, 'Unchained Melody is one of the most recorded songs of the 20th century, with over 500 versions in hundreds of different languages.

works.title: Ice Ice Baby
works.eventDescription: 'Ice Ice Baby', by Vanilla Ice became the first rap record to top the US singles chart, (and later also a UK No.1 single). The track was initially released as the B-side to the rapper's cover of 'Play That Funky Music', and became the A-side after US DJ's started playing the track.

works.title: Caribbean Queen
works.eventDescription: Billy Ocean started a two week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Caribbean Queen'. The song was originally called 'European Queen'.

works.title: No More Lonely Nights
works.eventDescription: Paul McCartney went to No.1 on the UK album chart with the film soundtrack to 'Give My Regards To Broad Street', featuring the UK No.2 single 'No More Lonely Nights.'

works.title: Pop Muzik
works.eventDescription: One Hit Wonder M went to No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Pop Muzik'. M was Robin Scott who scored one other UK top 40 hit, 'Pop Muzik' made No.2 in the UK.

works.title: Sorrow
works.eventDescription: David Bowie scored his second UK No.1 album when Pinups started a five-week run at the top of the charts. The set contained Bowie covering his favourite 60s songs; his version of The Mersey's 'Sorrow' made No.3 on the UK singles chart, (first recorded by The McCoys in 1965).

works.title: PinUps

works.title: She's Gone
works.eventDescription: Daryl Hall and John Oates released Abandoned Luncheonette. The most well-known track from the album 'She's Gone' did not become a hit when first released but gained momentum from two later covers, one by Lou Rawls, and one by Tavares. After the latter cover topped the Billboard R&B chart in 1974, the original was re-released and became a top 10 pop hit in 1976, reaching No. 7 in the US.

works.title: It’s Now or Never
works.eventDescription: Elvis Presley had his fifth UK No.1 single with It’s Now or Never, which stayed at No.1 for eight weeks. Based on the Italian song, 'O Sole Mio', it gave Presley his first post-army No.1.

works.title: Great Balls of Fire
